function: Learned joint control of AAV trajectory, RIS phase shifts, and ISAC beamforming matrices to maximize weighted sensing SNR and communication rate (p. 6).
system: AAV with 4 dual-functional antennas, 3 single-antenna users, one ground passive reflecting RIS with 64 elements; frequency band not stated (pp. 3, 9).
method: Multiagent deep reinforcement learning: DDPG for trajectory, TD3 for RIS phases, PPO for beamforming; penalty-based reward, centralized critic, 100 training episodes (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: LoS AAV links, Rician RIS-user links, Gauss-Markov channel evolution, path-loss exponent 2; no dataset or measurement described in Sec. IV (pp. 4, 7-8).
test_conditions: Training in the simulated environment (100 episodes); results are sweeps over RIS elements, users, antennas, thresholds, averaged over ten runs; no separate unseen test scenario stated (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Only learned: pure DDPG and pure PPO (called single-agent baselines), plus other DDPG/PPO/TD3 agent combinations in Table III; no non-learned method (pp. 10-12).
metrics: Total reward, average communication rate (bps/Hz), sensing SNR (dB), training convergence; t-tests over ten runs (pp. 9-12).
complexity: Order of training complexity O(Emax x N x (C_AAV + C_Beam + C_RIS)) in layer sizes; no FLOPs, parameters or runtime reported (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 8: "The simulation environment mimics a real-world scenario," i.e. a custom simulator with analytic LoS and Rician channels (p. 4); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or other standard model and no dataset in Sec. IV. The only mention of measured data is on p. 2 (cites [19]) and no data are described.
q2_support: p. 10: "Fig. 6 explores the effect of varying the number of users" is a parameter sweep; the paper never states that a policy trained in one configuration was tested in another or adapted, and results are averaged over ten simulation runs (p. 12).
q3_support: p. 10: "against the baseline methods (pure DDPG and pure PPO) under the balanced scenario" are the only comparisons (also Fig. 10, Table III); no non-learned method is compared, and p. 13 says future work will add benchmark methods from the literature.
q4_support: p. 8: "The computational complexity of the MADRL training" is analysed and gives O(Emax x N x (C_AAV + C_Beam + C_RIS)); it is the order of complexity of training only, with no FLOPs or runtime.
q5_support: p. 8: "The simulation environment mimics a real-world scenario," so a custom simulator; no code or data link and no availability statement appear anywhere in the paper, and the p. 2 mention of measured data [19] is not a release.
notes: Area: the learned method controls beams, RIS phases and the trajectory of an aerial base station that senses and communicates, so areas 5 and 6 both fit; area 6 chosen by the precedence 6 over 5 (aerial link that also senses). Reviewer to confirm. q1 and q5: p. 2 says the system was evaluated using real channel measurement data citing [19], but Sec. II-A, Sec. IV-A and Table II define an analytic channel and a simulated scenario and no measured data or campaign is described, so both are marked 0; reviewer to confirm. q3: pure DDPG and pure PPO may also be read as single-algorithm variants of the proposed design (p. 12), and in any case no non-learned baseline exists. q4 is training complexity only.
